comments.author: uyhgr
comments.story: LK99: Team of Southeast University observed zero resistance below 110 K
comments.why: Timestamped demo of hanging levitation from flux pinning
comments.text: Correct, the imperfections of the crystal allowing the flux pinning permits even a “hanging levitation”. Here is a timestamped video showing that: [VIDEO] If we develop methods of creating these superconductors with perfect crystal composition then there will only be the repulsion, allowing for levitation in a bowl shaped superconductor, but this “hanging levitation” would be impossible. Perhaps we will develop manufacturing techniques to induce specific imperfections into the material to ensure predictable flux pinning.

comments.author: trgern
comments.story: Room Temperature, Ambient Pressure Superconductivity–This Time for Real?
comments.why: Shows the locked-in effect of genuine quantum levitation
comments.text: The video of “levitation” is one of the things that makes me, a complete ignoramus of the subject matter, skeptical. [LINK] All other instances of “quantum levitation” that I have seen has a “locked in” effect: [VIDEO] . Whereas the material in this video seems to bounce and warble in a way that appears to me more akin to standard static or magnetic repulsion. Hope I’m wrong.

comments.author: jonmrodriguez
comments.story: How to Investigate a Flying Saucer
comments.why: Demonstrates levitating a type-II superconductor in a magnetic field
comments.text: I feel like part of the cultural fascination with flying saucers is that we intuitively feel like it should be possible for someone with advanced technology to levitate without expending power. We are starting to get there, with quantum locking, which can levitate a type-II superconductor relative to a supporting magnetic field. [VIDEO] [LINK] I wonder if it would be physically possible to utilize the Earth's extremely weak magnetic field to support any meaningful mass?
